newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-HINGIS POWERS INTO OPEN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS POWERS INTO OPEN FINAL.

text.p: Swiss teenager Martina Hingis charged into her first grand slam final with a crushing straight sets victory over American Mary Joe Fernandez in the semifinals of the Australian Open on Thursday.

Hingis was rarely troubled in a 6-1 6-3 victory over the American 14th seed. She meets Mary Pierce of France in Saturday's final for the chance to become the youngest grand slam champion in professional tennis history.
Hingis, 16, was in control of the match from the start breaking Fernandez's opening two service games to streak away to a 4-0 lead on her way to a comprehensive victory in 69 minutes.
Fernandez, the 14th seed, managed to hold her serve only twice in the entire match as Hingis rattled off a succession of forehand and backhand winners.
Hingis, who has not dropped a set in the tournament, suffered only two breaks of serve and showed rare signs of nerves when she faltered when serving for the match at 5-2 in the second set.
The Swiss world number four regained her composure and broke Fernandez's final service game, converting her third match point with an unreturnable forehand smash.
